speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) to what extent is the Network Capacity Factor able to address the widening gap between transport cost and fares; (b) how will the revised fare formula affect low-income and elderly Singaporeans; and (c) whether existing transport subsidy schemes for needy Singaporeans, such as concession holders who are Workfare Income Supplement recipients or senior citizens, will be reviewed or enhanced.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This helps inform their deliberations when they evaluate proposals from operators for fare changes and decide on the annual fare recommendations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The running costs of public transport operators are affected by a number of factors, including the price and quantity of the resources deployed.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For example, their expenditure on electricity in a particular year will depend on the quantity of electricity consumed during that year, and the prevailing electricity tariffs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: While the old fare formula adequately measured the changes in the price of resources consumed, it did not measure the changes in the quantity.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: When the capacity of the public transport network is quite stable from year to year, the limitation of the old fare formula is not material.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: However, as we aggressively expand the capacity of our public transport network, the inadequacy in the old fare formula will have a material impact on the sustainability of our public transport system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The limitation of the old fare formula has, therefore, contributed to a widening gap between fare revenue and operating costs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: So far, the yearly operating shortfall has been covered by Government subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: But, going forward, we need a fair way to take into account changes in the capacity of our public transport network relative to commuter demand.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: PTC designed the Network Capacity Factor (NCF) specifically to address the limitation in the old fare formula.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It will be positive where demand grows slower than capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Conversely, if capacity remains stagnant in a given year and demand grows faster than capacity, resulting in more crowded trains, NCF will be negative.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: PTC's mission is to ensure the long-term sustainability of our public transport system, while keeping fares affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As for our public transport fares, as Members have just heard from the Senior Parliamentary Secretary, the PTC will ensure that they remain affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In other words, transport fares are becoming more affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: PTC will also continue to review and, if necessary, enhance concession schemes to provide targeted help for specific groups like senior citizens, low-income individuals and persons with disabilities.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Linking the cost of building the bus network to commuters' fares under the new public transport, whether this approach to cost recovery will contradict our goal to be a car-lite society.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Because we are, on one hand, encouraging people to take public transport; on the other hand, when you put in more resources, then it will have an effect on the fares.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Because I hear the feedback, people say that NCF is very complicated.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The third question is why a service standard component is not added to the fare formula, only about cost recovery, but whether the service standard, can it be computed into the fare formula as well?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Our polices are argued thoroughly and sometimes debated in this House.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If there is a lack of understanding, we will continue to explain and publish them on the website, and so on.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: NCF it is a new factor, so I am not surprised that there may be some ignorance about it and people will need time to understand it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We will continue this education process but there is nothing opaque about it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The formula, the definition and how it is computed, it is all up there on the website.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In due course, towards the end of this year, when PTC has to evaluate the proposals coming in from the operators, and when the Fare Formula has to be quantified, I am quite sure they will go to great lengths to explain and justify how the factors are changing over the years, whether it is positive or negative.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, that part I can give the Member the assurance.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think that is how PTC intends to make use of this Factor.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If things improve through more comfortable ride, costs go up, then the Factor is positive.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That means there may be a need for fare adjustments.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Otherwise, the operators will find a gap in how to cover their operating costs.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: On the other hand, if the network is not expanding but demand is growing in a big way, more uncomfortable ride, then PTC will be asking for a fare reduction to counter this reduction in service level.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The first point by Er Dr Lee Bee Wah baffles me, I do not quite follow.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We expand our bus and rail network precisely so that we can facilitate car-lite.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, more buses, more trains and, hopefully, more people making use of public transport, less need to drive.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Then, we have an easier congestion problem on the roads.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: While we are encouraging people to take public transport, with this new fare formula, and several times the Minister had mentioned that the transport fare will surely go up, so the discussion on the ground is that while we encourage people to take public transport and then the transport fares keep going up, so is it going in the same direction?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: My follow-up supplementary question about this service level is whether the local service level will be picked up by this fare formula.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: For example, in Nee Soon South, we have Build-To-Order areas where residents keep complaining that, in the mornings, the wait is very long.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I understand because that bus service is a trunk bus service, but they said it is always packed and they have to wait for a long time.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, service level in this sense, will it be picked up by the fare formula?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Service level may not be picked up directly through the fare formula, but the sentiments will be picked up by me very quickly because Er Dr Lee Bee Wah will make sure that I fully understood what is happening on the ground.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am very attentive to this not just in Yishun but the whole of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But what I have said in Parliament several times is not that fares will definitely go up; that is not what I said.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: What I said is fares sometimes go down and sometimes go up.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It cannot be always going down, that is not possible, because a big part of our operating cost is manpower, unless you say, "Sorry, bus drivers, train drivers, your salary will forever be going down".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: With productivity, sometimes we can achieve some of this.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: You heard me many times in this House, in the last two and a half years, we are ramping up, intensifying maintenance, recruiting many more engineers, mechanics, technicians, and all those require money.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I really hope that Singaporeans understand that I want to do my job well, so that we can have a first-class transport system, and we will get there.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But I do need money because it is not realistic to hope that you get a good first-class reliable train with no need for any injection of resources.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, over time, in fact, affordability has improved.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Whatever we do, we will do what is necessary, including pumping in more resources in order to raise the standard of our public transport systems, so that people do not need to drive, but we need an adequate level of funding.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Either taxpayers through subsidy, or commuters through fare.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: To load it on one or the other is wrong, so it is a matter of co-sharing.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: PTC is given that task of doing this balancing act, finding a way to balance the interests of both sides.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: At the end of the day, remember, too, that many taxpayers are commuters and many commuters are also taxpayers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I refer to the PTC's news release on 22 March 2018 on the Fare Formula Review.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: There is a paragraph which says that "the Government will continue to provide significant subsidies for public transport services estimated to be around $9 billion over the next five years.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can the Minister provide some details on the nature of these subsidies?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Are there any details the Minister can share on which classes of commuters will benefit from these subsidies?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, over five years, that is about $5 billion.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, these are huge amounts of money coming from taxpayers and I think it is only fair that part of it must be borne or shared by commuters.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I have regularly compared and looked at the fares charged here versus Hong Kong, Taiwan, New York, London.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think Singaporeans, in their heart, when they travel, they know.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: PTC told me they do fairly frequent focus group discussions with the commuters, and they find our fares reasonable, and most of them say so.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In respect of service standard in NCF, would the Minister consider incorporating a measure of train reliability standard in order to incentivise the real operators to improve the reliability all round as well as also to manage commuters' expectation?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: After all, we hear a lot on the ground that there is expansion and there are supposed to be improved services.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But on the ground, people are still complaining about frequent delays.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I have been in this game now for two and a half years and I personally witnessed how things have changed.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Yes, last year, we had an awful year, especially towards the end of last year.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Two incidents, which should not have happened, happened unfortunately.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But there was a silver lining to it; out of it, we came up with Early Closure Late Opening (ECLO).

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As I always shared with my transport colleagues, ECLO is our favourite four-letter word because that allows us to intensify engineering maintenance.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Since December, and we are now approaching the middle of May, the situation has improved significantly.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, when the Member said the commuters are upset over very frequent delays, it depends on when you asked them.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I do not know whether the Member uses trains and buses.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I meet many more commuters than he does, I think.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: North-South line, for example, which used to have a lot of problems with rail reliability, goes through my constituency.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In my many house-to-house visits, it used to be about trains.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But, in the last few months, I have not heard about trains.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Instead, it is e-scooters and bicycles being thrown all over the place.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, as far as rail is concerned, things have improved.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Bus level improvements I think have been pretty obvious in the last two to three years.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Of course, we are not yet in a perfect situation, like in Yishun, but things will get better, I am quite sure.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As to whether we should include rail reliability into the formula, first of all, this formula is not set by me.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: PTC, after consulting their members, consulting Singaporeans, came up with this formula.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They did think about whether to include rail reliability.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But in the end, they decided against it for various reasons.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In any case, even though it is not in the fare formula, I deal with it directly, myself, through the sort of focus and pressure I exert on the operators to make sure they work on rail reliability because that is my priority.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And I will see to it that it happens, whether or not it is included in the fare formula.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And if you punish them through reduced fares, you are withdrawing resources from the operators.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And you will be doing exactly the wrong thing.
